question: Who led Alloy Robotics' latest funding round?

Its agents analyze robot data and surface the patterns that matter, so engineers spend less time digging through the last run and more time building the next. hits.title: Alloy Robotics emerges from stealth with $4.5m pre-seed raise
hits.snippet: Alloy Robotics was founded eight months ago by Joe Harris, the former Chief Commercial Officer of Eucalyptus. Up until now, the company has been in stealth mode. But on the back of a $4.5m pre-seed raise led by Blackbird alongside Airtree Ventures, Skip Capital, and Bay Area VC Xtal Ventures, Harris is ready to talk.

hits.title: Alloy Robotics Raises $8M in New Funding to Help Engineers Debug Robot Fleets With AI Agents
hits.snippet: - Alloy Robotics raised $8 million at an $80 million valuation to expand its AI-agent platform for diagnosing robot failures and improving fleet reliability. - Square Peg led the round, with participation from Blackbird, Airtree, Skip Capital and executives and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter and Carbon Robotics. - Alloy said its platform supports nearly 1,000 robots and has analyzed more than 10,000 missions, combining logs, telemetry, video and engineering context while also connecting with coding agents such as Codex and Claude Code through Model Context Protocol. ... Leading the funding round was Square Peg with participation from existing investors Blackbird, Airtree and Skip Capital, according to Alloy. The financing also included executives and engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Tesla, Waymo, Halter and Carbon Robotics.

hits.title: Alloy Robotics Raises $11.5m at $115m Valuation | Joe Harris posted on the topic | LinkedIn
hits.snippet: Today, we’re announcing another A$11.5m at a A$115m valuation 🤖 Bringing our total raised to over A$16m. The round was led by Square Peg, with continued support from Blackbird Airtree, Skip Capital and an incredible group of angels, founders and leaders from Tesla, Waymo, OpenAI, Anthropic and more. The investor support means a lot. But the signal that gave me the confidence to raise again came from our customers. A full day of robot test analysis now takes ten minutes. At Advanced Navigation, that has helped the validation team go from two tests per week to ten. Questions that once took weeks can now be answered the same day. Results like these are why Alloy Robotics has raised again, barely one year after we started. 🚀 Since launching publicly late last year, we have deployed Alloy across agriculture, defence, drones, medical devices, industrial systems, maritime robotics and humanoids. And we have learned something important: Robotics teams are not short of data. They are short on memory. The context needed to understand a robot is scattered across logs, images, tickets, code and the heads of individual engineers. When something fails, teams piece that context together manually.

hits.title: Alloy raises $4.5m to solve robotics data challenge | Joe Harris posted on the topic | LinkedIn
hits.snippet: It's official 🤖 I'm excited to announce Alloy, and our $4.5m pre-seed round led by Blackbird with support from Airtree, Xtal, Skip Capital and an incredible group of angels, leaders and founders of Tesla, Waymo, Carbon Robotics, Halter, Reach Robotics, Relevance AI and more. One of the strongest pre-seed rounds ever done in Australia and a testament to the calibre of the team and magnitude of the opportunity. At Alloy, we are building the system for robotics companies to reduce time spent on processing data by up to 90%, enabling 10x faster iteration. Instead of leaving behind 99% of their data in cold storage, teams can continuously improve performance. This is one of the most pressing problems in robotics: robotics teams are drowning in terabytes of data they can't efficiently search or analyze, forcing every company to build expensive custom infrastructure from scratch. And the problem only gets worse as you scale. When your robot encounters an issue, has it occurred before? How frequently? Will you know if it happens again?
